scope: Actual local native init-block join, production dump create and publish, bootstrap of a separate never-started identity, and two-pass native installed-state readback.

native_build.relationship_to_published_source: All validator, validator-engine, crypto and top-level CMake source files are byte-identical to the published implementation. Later commits change the Python/Rust test harness, CI and documentation. The binary retains the native build revision rather than claiming it was rebuilt at the later harness commit.
native_build.profile: CMake Release, Clang 21.1.8, Linux x86_64, RocksDB and jemalloc enabled
native_build.rust_profile: Rust 1.97.1 dev/test, native and native-lifecycle-tests features; normal worker production sources unchanged by this work
native_build.namespace_isolation: Native worker validation used separate user and network namespaces. The container default sandbox cannot map uid 0, so local execution used the environment escalation mechanism without bypassing the validation isolation.

upstream_comparison.result: The inherited scheduler still chooses Random::fast(0, 3600 * 6). Its engine CLI has no immediate local-test serialization control. The new explicit local-only option leaves that default expression unchanged.

genesis_native_tests.includes: Real PQ-key/Fift generation, absent-by-default Config36, exact interval/count/weight/descriptor checks, missing-Config36 mutation red then restored green, invalid bounds and nonlocal refusal.

ci_guard_tests.includes: Ten omission/comment-out cases for the new executable command, environment and three required markers; narrow always-upload exception; bounded private-file-excluding failure logs.

results.format_and_static_checks: Changed-file Ruff check/format, changed-line clang-format, Rustfmt and git diff --check passed. Targeted basedpyright reported zero errors; inherited gradual-typing warnings remain.

mutation.mutation: omit held nonzero init from native anchor_set; keep zero-state proof

native_sensitivity.required_failure: create did not prove its held init block
native_sensitivity.reason_old_zero_only_fixture_is_insensit: When held.init equals held.zero, removing held.init from a set changes nothing. The real joined source has distinct nonzero init 192, so the new native regression fails at the omitted proof.

omission_control: Preserve the normal worker binary. In tosctl/src/node-control/node-data-sync/src/native_validation.rs replace exactly the recorded anchor_set line, run cargo build --manifest-path tosctl/src/Cargo.toml --locked -p node-data-sync --features native --bin node-data-sync-worker, and preserve that mutant worker separately.
Restore the source file before compiling/running the lifecycle test. Point NODE_SYNC_NATIVE_WORKER at the mutant: require exit 101 and the exact held-init proof assertion, with no success marker.
Point NODE_SYNC_NATIVE_WORKER at the preserved normal worker and repeat the same native test: require one pass, zero failures and PRODUCTION_INIT_BLOCK_PUBLISH_BOOTSTRAP_OK.

resource_and_boundary_review.native_state: Two fixed boolean option fields and shared virtual dispatch entries; no new container, queue, actor, retained buffer, file descriptor, or resource lifetime. The existing serializer timer uses zero delay only after loaded on-chain global_id 3 admission; public defaults are unchanged.
resource_and_boundary_review.harness: Four local validators, one joining observer, one never-started target; finite read/capture deadlines and 15-minute CI fixture timeout. Expected fatal controls disable core dumps. Captured source data was 1590897 bytes; database preallocation and debug workers remained disposable local build/run output.
resource_and_boundary_review.identity: Source keys unchanged; receiver keys distinct and preserved; exact receiver config bytes checked at the reached pre-start boundary, then full semantic equality after only native out_port 0 to 3278 and absent to empty GC expansion.
resource_and_boundary_review.test_adapters: The initial capture uses two real live validator RPC references. The lifecycle uses the existing manager/reference test adapters; manager starts actual native engines, and all storage/ancestry/installed-state validation runs through the actual worker and engine.

evidence_retention.committed: Only this result index and bounded essential join/red/green output excerpts are committed. Trailing whitespace and surplus final blank lines are normalized; the exact red failure and native success content remain preserved without relying on inaccessible raw-log hashes.
evidence_retention.ci: native-init-block-publisher-<commit> artifact retains join receipt, initial native validation JSON and lifecycle output for 14 days; bounded node failure logs are collected separately. Node keys and database trees are excluded.

pre_anchor_proof_control.purpose: Required red-before control: the same init-block join, create/publish and third-node bootstrap test fails on the validation path used before backward anchor proofs, then passes with the normal worker.
pre_anchor_proof_control.environment: Native build of this commit (CMake Release, Clang 21.1.8, RocksDB and jemalloc); Rust dev profile, bfd linker, 4 build jobs at the lowest priority under a CPU-temperature pause guard (paused six times for at most 6 s each).
pre_anchor_proof_control.mutation: restore the held zero-state GetState read and the LookupBlock ancestry loop in place of the backward anchor proofs
pre_anchor_proof_control.red_failure: production create rejected init-block source; worker: native recovery or required shard-state read did not complete; last check: native GetState for held zero state (-1,8000000000000000,0):E691E357...: native state read failed (651): zerostate not in db
pre_anchor_proof_control.raw_output_note: output_sha256 values are of the complete raw test outputs; the committed excerpts start at the test run, with trailing whitespace and surplus final blank lines removed.
pre_anchor_proof_control.ci: branch-chain-python.yml runs the same runner after the native lifecycle suite and requires INIT_BLOCK_PRE_ANCHOR_CONTROL_OK.
